components.note: 灬 (fire dots) — fire and heat: 热, 点, 煮, 照; 黑 is soot and smoke from a flame.
巾 (cloth) — cloth, as in 布, 带, 帽: 帮 first meant the side of a shoe.
邦 (bāng, nation) gives the exact sound; 邦 itself means state or country.

example.hanzi: 这部电影讲述了黑帮之间的斗争。
example.pinyin: Zhè bù diànyǐng jiǎngshùle hēibāng zhījiān de dòuzhēng.
example.english: This movie tells the story of a struggle between criminal gangs.
example.fact: The Sicilian Mafia is believed to have emerged in the mid-19th century, partly as informal groups of armed guards hired by absentee landowners to protect citrus and wheat estates from bandits, gradually evolving into organized criminal networks with their own codes of conduct. American Prohibition in the 1920s later gave organized crime groups in the United States, like Al Capone's Chicago outfit, a massive new revenue stream from illegal alcohol.

examples.hanzi: 他在黑帮电影里演过老大。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài hēibāng diànyǐng lǐ yǎn guo lǎodà.
examples.english: He played a boss in a gangster movie.

examples.hanzi: 我喜欢看黑帮题材的电影。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan kàn hēibāng tícái de diànyǐng.
examples.english: I like watching gangster-themed movies.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh, 肉月旁) — the body-part radical, as in 脸, 腿, 脑; 肩 is the shoulder.
⺼ (flesh, 肉月旁) — body-part radical, as in 脸, 腿; 膀 is the upper arm or shoulder.
旁 (páng) is a loose hint for bǎng; 榜 bǎng and 磅 bàng share it.

example.hanzi: 他把包扛在肩膀上。
example.pinyin: Tā bǎ bāo káng zài jiānbǎng shàng.
example.english: He carried the bag on his shoulder.
example.fact: The shoulder is the most mobile joint in the human body, able to rotate through a wider range of motion than any other joint, largely because the socket is shallow compared to joints like the hip. That mobility comes at a cost, though — the shoulder is also one of the most frequently dislocated joints, precisely because its loose-fitting design trades stability for a wider range of movement.

examples.hanzi: 她靠在我的肩膀上睡着了。
examples.pinyin: Tā kào zài wǒ de jiānbǎng shàng shuìzháo le.
examples.english: She fell asleep leaning on my shoulder.

examples.hanzi: 他拍了拍我的肩膀，说谢谢。
examples.pinyin: Tā pāi le pāi wǒ de jiānbǎng, shuō xièxie.
examples.english: He patted my shoulder and said thanks.

components.note: 宀 (roof, house) — 宀 is a roof, as in 家 home, 室 room, 安 safe; 宣 was a large hall, where proclamations are made.
亻 (person) — person radical — 传 is something passed from person to person.
专 (zhuān) — near sound — 传 is chuán; 专 also sounds out 转 zhuǎn and 砖 zhuān.

example.hanzi: 政府发布了新的宣传海报。
example.pinyin: Zhèngfǔ fābùle xīn de xuānchuán hǎibào.
example.english: The government released a new propaganda poster.
example.fact: The famous 'I Want YOU for U.S. Army' recruitment poster, depicting Uncle Sam pointing directly at the viewer, was created by illustrator James Montgomery Flagg during World War I and reused during World War II, becoming one of the most reproduced images in American history. Flagg reportedly used his own face as a model for Uncle Sam to save money on hiring someone else.

examples.hanzi: 这家商店在网上做宣传。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā shāngdiàn zài wǎngshàng zuò xuānchuán.
examples.english: This store does promotion online.

examples.hanzi: 学校宣传环保的重要性。
examples.pinyin: Xuéxiào xuānchuán huánbǎo de zhòngyàoxìng.
examples.english: The school promotes the importance of environmental protection.

components.note: 厂 (cliff) — the visible frame, as in 原, 厚. Memory aid: a stern cliff face — 严重 serious, 严格 strict. Cliff family hint, not proven.
嚴 (traditional) — a larger shape with two mouths 吅 shouting orders. 严 cut it to 亚 plus 厂, losing the clue.
木 (wood, tree) — wood radical — 格 first meant a wooden frame or lattice, hence "pattern, standard"; compare 树 tree, 板 board.
各 (gè) — same syllable, different tone — 格 is gé; 各 also sounds out 阁 gé and 胳 gē.

example.hanzi: 这所学校对学生的纪律要求非常严格。
example.pinyin: Zhè suǒ xuéxiào duì xuésheng de jìlǜ yāoqiú fēicháng yángé.
example.english: This school has very strict discipline requirements for students.
example.fact: Ancient Sparta subjected boys as young as seven to an extraordinarily strict state-run training system called the agoge, which emphasized physical endurance, deliberate hardship like minimal food and clothing, and unquestioning obedience to prepare them for a lifetime as soldiers. The system was so demanding and singularly focused on producing warriors that Sparta, despite its military reputation, left behind comparatively little literature, art, or architecture compared to other Greek city-states.

examples.hanzi: 我妈妈对我很严格。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ māma duì wǒ hěn yángé.
examples.english: My mom is very strict with me.

examples.hanzi: 这家工厂有严格的安全规定。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngchǎng yǒu yángé de ānquán guīdìng.
examples.english: This factory has strict safety rules.

components.note: 将 (jiāng) is the trimmed top part: 奖 jiǎng sounds like 桨 jiǎng and 浆 jiāng.
力 (strength) — marks effort, as in 动 move, 努 strive, 办; 励 is to urge on.
厉 (lì) gives the sound exactly: 励 lì.

example.hanzi: 公司给表现优秀的员工发放了奖励。
example.pinyin: Gōngsī gěi biǎoxiàn yōuxiù de yuángōng fāfàngle jiǎnglì.
example.english: The company gave rewards to employees with excellent performance.
example.fact: Psychologist B.F. Skinner's mid-20th-century experiments with pigeons and rats in 'Skinner boxes' showed that behavior reinforced by rewards, even irregular or unpredictable ones, tends to be repeated more persistently than behavior rewarded every single time. This principle, called operant conditioning, later influenced everything from classroom teaching methods to the variable reward mechanics used in modern slot machines and mobile games.

examples.hanzi: 考了第一名，老师给了我一份奖励。
examples.pinyin: Kǎo le dì yī míng, lǎoshī gěi le wǒ yí fèn jiǎnglì.
examples.english: I got first place, and the teacher gave me a reward.

examples.hanzi: 这个小孩做完作业就奖励自己看动画片。
examples.pinyin: Zhège xiǎohái zuò wán zuòyè jiù jiǎnglì zìjǐ kàn dònghuàpiàn.
examples.english: After finishing his homework, this kid rewards himself by watching cartoons.

components.note: 心 (heart) — 心 marks feelings, as in 想, 爱, 怒; 悲 is sorrow.
非 (fēi) — near sound — 悲 is bēi; 非 also sounds out 辈 bèi and 排 pái.
刂 (knife) — 刂 is 刀 (knife), as in 到, 别, 利; 剧 first meant to cut deeply, then intense and drama.
居 (jū) — near sound — 剧 is jù; 居 also sounds out 据 jù.

example.hanzi: 泰坦尼克号的沉没是二十世纪最著名的悲剧之一。
example.pinyin: Tàitǎnníkè hào de chénmò shì èrshí shìjì zuì zhùmíng de bēijù zhī yī.
example.english: The sinking of the Titanic is one of the most famous tragedies of the 20th century.
example.fact: The Titanic sank in the early hours of April 15, 1912, after striking an iceberg in the North Atlantic on its maiden voyage from Southampton to New York. More than 1,500 of the roughly 2,224 people aboard died, largely because the ship carried lifeboats for only about half its passengers and crew. The wreck was not located until 1985, resting about 3,800 meters below the surface, and its discovery reshaped maritime safety regulations that still apply today.

examples.hanzi: 这个故事的结局是个悲剧。
examples.pinyin: Zhège gùshi de jiéjú shì ge bēijù.
examples.english: The ending of this story is a tragedy.

examples.hanzi: 我们不想让这样的悲剧再发生。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen bù xiǎng ràng zhèyàng de bēijù zài fāshēng.
examples.english: We don't want such a tragedy to happen again.

components.note: 买 (simplified 買) — the old form shows a net 网 over a shell 贝 (money): netting goods, to buy. 卖 mài sell is built on 买.
买 (mǎi, buy) — its sound is almost the same as 卖 mài, and the meaning is the opposite: buy and sell.

example.hanzi: 丝绸之路曾经是东西方之间买卖货物的重要通道。
example.pinyin: Sīchóu zhī Lù céngjīng shì dōngxī fāng zhījiān mǎimài huòwù de zhòngyào tōngdào.
example.english: The Silk Road was once an important route for buying and selling goods between East and West.
example.fact: The Silk Road was not a single road but a network of trade routes connecting China to the Mediterranean, stretching over 6,000 kilometers and active from roughly 130 BC to the 1450s. Beyond silk, traders carried spices, paper, gunpowder, and religious ideas across the continent, and the exchange helped spread Buddhism from India into China. The route also inadvertently helped spread the Black Death into Europe in the 14th century.

examples.hanzi: 他在市场上做小买卖。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài shìchǎng shàng zuò xiǎo mǎimai.
examples.english: He runs a small business at the market.

examples.hanzi: 这笔买卖你亏了。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bǐ mǎimai nǐ kuī le.
examples.english: You lost out on this deal.

components.note: 交 (cross, hand over) — a person with legs crossed: to intersect, then to exchange. Same part in 校 xiào, 较 jiào, 胶 jiāo.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 话.
炎 (yán) is a close sound clue for tán; 炎 also sounds out 淡 dàn and 痰 tán.

example.hanzi: 两位科学家在会议休息时间友好地交谈起来。
example.pinyin: Liǎng wèi kēxuéjiā zài huìyì xiūxi shíjiān yǒuhǎo de jiāotán qǐlái.
example.english: The two scientists struck up a friendly conversation during the conference break.
example.fact: The 1927 Solvay Conference in Brussels brought together 29 of the era's leading physicists, including Einstein, Bohr, and Curie, to debate the new theory of quantum mechanics. Seventeen of the attendees were or later became Nobel Prize winners. The informal conversations there, especially the ongoing debate between Einstein and Bohr about the nature of reality, shaped the direction of physics for decades afterward.

examples.hanzi: 他们在咖啡店里交谈了一个小时。
examples.pinyin: Tāmen zài kāfēidiàn lǐ jiāotán le yí ge xiǎoshí.
examples.english: They talked in the cafe for an hour.

examples.hanzi: 老师想和你单独交谈一下。
examples.pinyin: Lǎoshī xiǎng hé nǐ dāndú jiāotán yíxià.
examples.english: The teacher would like to talk with you alone.

components.note: 弓 (bow) — the vertical stroke 丨 is the string being drawn back on a bow — 引 is to pull, then to attract and to cite.
手 (hand) — marks hand actions, as in 拿, 打, 拉; 擎 is to hold up, as in 引擎.
敬 (jìng) is only a loose sound hint for qíng.

example.hanzi: 这辆老式汽车的引擎发出低沉的轰鸣声。
example.pinyin: Zhè liàng lǎoshì qìchē de yǐnqíng fāchū dīchén de hōngmíng shēng.
example.english: The old car's engine let out a deep rumbling roar.
example.fact: The first practical internal combustion engine is credited to Nikolaus Otto, who built a working four-stroke gas engine in 1876 in Germany. That four-stroke cycle — intake, compression, combustion, exhaust — still powers the vast majority of gasoline engines today. Karl Benz later adapted a similar engine to build the Benz Patent-Motorwagen in 1885, widely regarded as the first true automobile.

examples.hanzi: 汽车的引擎出了问题。
examples.pinyin: Qìchē de yǐnqíng chū le wèntí.
examples.english: There is something wrong with the car's engine.

examples.hanzi: 这台引擎非常省油。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tái yǐnqíng fēicháng shěng yóu.
examples.english: This engine is very fuel-efficient.

components.note: ⺼ (flesh, 肉月旁) — the body-part radical, as in 脸, 腿, 脑; 膝 is the knee.
桼 (qī) is a loose hint for xī; 漆 qī shares it.
皿 (dish) — marks vessels, as in 盘, 盒, 盆; 盖 is a lid, a cover over a vessel.

example.hanzi: 她跑步时不小心摔倒,擦伤了膝盖。
example.pinyin: Tā pǎobù shí bù xiǎoxīn shuāidǎo, cāshāng le xīgài.
example.english: She fell while running and scraped her knee.
example.fact: The knee is the largest joint in the human body and one of the most complex, relying on four major ligaments and two C-shaped cartilage pads called menisci to stay stable. It's also one of the most commonly injured joints in sports, with the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) alone responsible for an estimated 100,000-plus reconstructive surgeries in the United States each year. Unlike most joints, the kneecap (patella) is a separate floating bone embedded in a tendon rather than connected directly to another bone.

examples.hanzi: 爬了一天山，我的膝盖很疼。
examples.pinyin: Pá le yì tiān shān, wǒ de xīgài hěn téng.
examples.english: After climbing the mountain all day, my knees hurt.

examples.hanzi: 他蹲下来，膝盖碰到了地板。
examples.pinyin: Tā dūn xiàlai, xīgài pèng dào le dìbǎn.
examples.english: He crouched down and his knee touched the floor.

components.note: 辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过 pass, 进 enter, 送 send; to meet is to cross paths.
禺 (yú) is close to yù; same part in 愚 yú and 偶 ǒu.

example.hanzi: 我在路上遇到了老同学。
example.pinyin: Wǒ zài lù shàng yùdào le lǎo tóngxué.
example.english: I ran into an old classmate on the road.
example.fact: 遇 seldom stands alone: 遇到 and 遇见 mean 'to run into', while 遇 implies an unplanned meeting. For problems you can also say 遇到困难 ('to run into difficulty').

examples.hanzi: 我昨天在超市遇见了老师。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuótiān zài chāoshì yùjiàn le lǎoshī.
examples.english: I ran into my teacher at the supermarket yesterday.

examples.hanzi: 你遇到困难可以找我。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yùdào kùnnan kěyǐ zhǎo wǒ.
examples.english: If you run into difficulties, you can come to me.

components.note: 卩 (kneeling person) — a hand 爪 pressing on a person 卩: to stamp or press a mark, hence seal and print.
⺮ (bamboo) — bamboo slips, once used for writing and lists, as in 等 wait, 笔 pen, 笑 laugh.
弟 (dì) gives the exact sound; 弟 also sounds out 梯 tī and 剃 tì.
宀 (roof) — houses and shelter, as in 家, 字, 室.
女 (woman) — a woman at home under the roof: calm and safe.

example.hanzi: 印第安部落的传统文化至今仍受到许多人的尊重和研究。
example.pinyin: Yìndì'ān bùluò de chuántǒng wénhuà zhìjīn réng shòudào xǔduō rén de zūnjìng hé yánjiū.
example.english: The traditional culture of Native American tribes is still respected and studied by many people today.
example.fact: The name 'Indian' for Native Americans traces back to Christopher Columbus, who mistakenly believed he had reached the East Indies in 1492. Today the Americas are home to hundreds of distinct Indigenous nations, each with its own language, government, and history that predate European contact by thousands of years. The Cahokia Mounds near modern St. Louis, built by Indigenous peoples around 1050 AD, once housed a city larger than London at the time.

examples.hanzi: 这位作家写过关于印第安人的书。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi zuòjiā xiě guo guānyú Yìndì'ān rén de shū.
examples.english: This writer has written books about Native Americans.

examples.hanzi: 那部电影讲的是印第安人的生活。
examples.pinyin: Nà bù diànyǐng jiǎng de shì Yìndì'ān rén de shēnghuó.
examples.english: That film is about the life of Native Americans.

components.note: 讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 话.
炎 (yán) is a close sound clue for tán; 炎 also sounds out 淡 dàn and 痰 tán.
刂 (knife) — 刂 is 刀 (knife) as in 到, 别, 利; 判 is to cut in half, so to separate and decide.
半 (bàn) — near sound — 判 is pàn; 半 means half.

example.hanzi: 双方经过长时间的谈判,终于达成了协议。
example.pinyin: Shuāngfāng jīngguò cháng shíjiān de tánpàn, zhōngyú dáchéng le xiéyì.
example.english: After lengthy negotiations, both sides finally reached an agreement.
example.fact: The Camp David Accords of 1978 were the result of thirteen days of secretive, intensive negotiation between Egyptian President Anwar Sadat and Israeli Prime Minister Menachem Begin, mediated by U.S. President Jimmy Carter. The talks nearly collapsed multiple times before producing a peace treaty the following year, ending decades of formal war between the two countries. Sadat and Begin were jointly awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1978 for the breakthrough.

examples.hanzi: 双方明天继续谈判。
examples.pinyin: Shuāngfāng míngtiān jìxù tánpàn.
examples.english: The two sides will continue negotiating tomorrow.

examples.hanzi: 这次谈判很不顺利。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì tánpàn hěn bú shùnlì.
examples.english: This round of negotiations did not go smoothly.

meanings: measure word for streams, scents, forces

components.note: ⺼ (flesh, form of 月) — body parts: 腿 leg, 脚 foot, 肚 belly; 股 is the thigh or rump, later a share.
殳 (shū, weapon in hand) — only a loose sound hint; it also appears in 投 and 设.

example.hanzi: 厨房里飘来一股香味。
example.pinyin: Chúfáng lǐ piāolái yì gǔ xiāngwèi.
example.english: A whiff of something delicious drifted from the kitchen.
example.fact: As a measure word 股 counts things that flow or rise: 一股香味 (a scent), 一股力量 (a surge of strength). It also means 'share', which is why 股票 are stocks and 股东 are shareholders.

examples.hanzi: 一股冷风吹进了房间。
examples.pinyin: Yì gǔ lěngfēng chuī jìn le fángjiān.
examples.english: A gust of cold wind blew into the room.

examples.hanzi: 他买了一些公司的股票。
examples.pinyin: Tā mǎi le yìxiē gōngsī de gǔpiào.
examples.english: He bought some of the company's stock.

components.note: 彡 (patterns, hairlines) — marks shape, shadow and decoration, as in 影 shadow, 彩 colour; 形 is a shape.
开 (a worn-down 幵) hints at the sound: 形 xíng sounds like 刑 and 型.

example.hanzi: 这个盒子是圆形的。
example.pinyin: Zhège hézi shì yuánxíng de.
example.english: This box is round-shaped.
example.fact: 形 attaches to shape words: 圆形 (circle), 方形 (square), 形状 (shape). In grammar 形容词 is the 'adjective', literally a word that 'describes form'.

examples.hanzi: 我想要一个心形的蛋糕。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng yào yí ge xīnxíng de dàngāo.
examples.english: I'd like a heart-shaped cake.

examples.hanzi: 这个城市的地形很复杂。
examples.pinyin: Zhège chéngshì de dìxíng hěn fùzá.
examples.english: This city's terrain is very complicated.

components.note: 疒 (illness) — marks sickness, as in 病 ill, 疼 pain, 痛 ache; 瘦 is thin, with 叟 (elder) as sound.
叟 (sǒu) — loose sound hint (shòu); 叟 also sounds out 搜 sōu and 艘 sōu.

example.hanzi: 他最近瘦了很多。
example.pinyin: Tā zuìjìn shòu le hěn duō.
example.english: He has lost a lot of weight recently.
example.fact: 瘦 contrasts with 胖 for people and with 肥 for meat (瘦肉 lean meat vs 肥肉 fatty meat). With clothes it means 'tight-fitting': 这件衣服太瘦了.

examples.hanzi: 这条裤子有点瘦,我穿不进去。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo kùzi yǒudiǎn shòu, wǒ chuān bu jìnqù.
examples.english: These pants are a bit tight; I can't get into them.

examples.hanzi: 她为了变瘦每天跑步。
examples.pinyin: Tā wèile biàn shòu měitiān pǎobù.
examples.english: She runs every day to get slimmer.

components.note: 医 (doctor) — simplified from 醫, which had 酉 (medicinal wine, as in 酒) at the bottom; the box 匚 and arrow 矢 remain.
子 (child) — a child learning under a roof: the top shows hands over a house, and the child 子 below. Also gives 觉 jué its upper part.

example.hanzi: 他从小就对医学充满兴趣,长大后成为了一名外科医生。
example.pinyin: Tā cóngxiǎo jiù duì yīxué chōngmǎn xìngqù, zhǎngdà hòu chéngwéi le yī míng wàikē yīshēng.
example.english: He was fascinated by medicine from childhood and grew up to become a surgeon.
example.fact: Penicillin, the world's first widely used antibiotic, was discovered somewhat by accident in 1928 when Alexander Fleming noticed a mold contaminating one of his bacterial culture plates had killed the surrounding bacteria. It took another decade before Howard Florey and Ernst Chain developed methods to mass-produce it, just in time to treat wounded soldiers in World War II. The discovery is credited with saving hundreds of millions of lives and marked the start of the modern antibiotic era.

examples.hanzi: 她在大学里学医学。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài dàxué lǐ xué yīxué.
examples.english: She studies medicine at university.

examples.hanzi: 现代医学让很多病人恢复了健康。
examples.pinyin: Xiàndài yīxué ràng hěn duō bìngrén huīfù le jiànkāng.
examples.english: Modern medicine has helped many patients recover.

components.note: 人 (person) — the right-hand part. The left part is a hook-and-dot, from an old tool-like shape. Meaning 'by means of, so as to' is not shown by the parts today.
Memory aid: a person 人 using a tool to get something done — 'by means of' (可以, 所以, 以前). A mnemonic, not proven etymology.
下 (below) — a mark placed under a line, the mirror of 上 above.

example.hanzi: 请仔细阅读以下几点注意事项。
example.pinyin: Qǐng zǐxì yuèdú yǐxià jǐ diǎn zhùyì shìxiàng.
example.english: Please carefully read the following points of caution.
example.fact: Standardized safety instructions like pre-flight briefings trace back to the 1930s, when early airlines began requiring crew to explain emergency exits and equipment before takeoff. The International Civil Aviation Organization later codified these requirements globally after World War II. Studies by aviation safety researchers have found that passengers who watch safety briefings, rather than tuning them out, have measurably better outcomes locating exits during real evacuations.

examples.hanzi: 十八岁以下的孩子不能进去。
examples.pinyin: Shíbā suì yǐxià de háizi bù néng jìnqù.
examples.english: Children under eighteen are not allowed in.

examples.hanzi: 今天最低气温在零度以下。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān zuìdī qìwēn zài língdù yǐxià.
examples.english: Today's lowest temperature is below zero.

components.note: 日 (sun, day) — a picture of the sun, once round with a dot, now squared off. As a radical it marks light and time: 明, 晴, 时.
讠 (speech) — words and language, as in 说, 请, 谢; 记 is to note down or remember.
己 (jǐ) is a close sound clue for jì; 己 also sounds out 纪 jì and 起 qǐ.

example.hanzi: 安妮·弗兰克在躲藏期间写下了著名的日记。
example.pinyin: Ānnī·Fúlánkè zài duǒcáng qījiān xiěxià le zhùmíng de rìjì.
example.english: Anne Frank wrote her famous diary while she was in hiding.
example.fact: Anne Frank kept her diary from 1942 to 1944 while hiding with her family in a concealed annex behind a bookcase in Amsterdam during the Nazi occupation of the Netherlands. She received the diary, a checkered notebook, as a 13th birthday present just weeks before her family went into hiding. First published in 1947 by her father Otto Frank, the only family member to survive the camps, it has since been translated into more than 70 languages.

examples.hanzi: 我每天晚上都写日记。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān wǎnshang dōu xiě rìjì.
examples.english: I write in my diary every night.

examples.hanzi: 她把旅行的经历记在日记里。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ lǚxíng de jīnglì jì zài rìjì lǐ.
examples.english: She wrote down her travel experiences in her diary.

components.note: 阝 (hill, from 阜) — marks walls and slopes, as in 院, 阶, 附; 隔 is to separate with a partition.
鬲 (gé) gives the sound exactly: 隔 gé.
土 (earth) — marks soil and earthen things, as in 墙 wall, 地, 城; 壁 is a wall.
辟 (pì) hints at the sound: 壁 bì is close to 臂 bì and 避 bì, which share it.

example.hanzi: 隔壁邻居家养了一只非常吵闹的狗。
example.pinyin: Gébì línjū jiā yǎng le yī zhī fēicháng chǎonào de gǒu.
example.english: The neighbor next door has a very noisy dog.
example.fact: Sound insulation between apartments depends heavily on a building's construction, and older buildings with plaster and lath walls often transmit far more noise than modern ones using resilient channels and mass-loaded vinyl. Studies on urban noise complaints consistently rank barking dogs and loud neighbors among the top sources of disputes between residents. Some cities, like Berlin, even employ mediators specifically trained to resolve neighbor noise conflicts before they reach court.

examples.hanzi: 我的好朋友住在隔壁。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de hǎo péngyou zhù zài gébì.
examples.english: My good friend lives next door.

examples.hanzi: 隔壁房间有人在唱歌。
examples.pinyin: Gébì fángjiān yǒu rén zài chàng gē.
examples.english: Someone is singing in the next room.

components.note: 艹 (grass) — plants; 蕾 is a flower bud, as in 花 flower, 草 grass.
雷 (léi) gives a close sound; it also sounds out 擂 léi and 镭 léi.

example.hanzi: 花园里的花蕾快开了。
example.pinyin: Huāyuán lǐ de huālěi kuài kāi le.
example.english: The flower buds in the garden are about to open.
example.fact: 蕾 is rarely used on its own; it appears in 花蕾 or 蓓蕾 (bud), and in 味蕾, the word for 'taste buds' on the tongue. 蓓蕾 is also used figuratively for young talent.

examples.hanzi: 玫瑰的花蕾慢慢地开了。
examples.pinyin: Méigui de huālěi mànmàn de kāi le.
examples.english: The rosebuds slowly opened.

examples.hanzi: 这个芭蕾舞演员很有名。
examples.pinyin: Zhège bālěiwǔ yǎnyuán hěn yǒumíng.
examples.english: This ballet dancer is very famous.

components.note: 辶 (walk, 走之旁) — movement and roads: 过, 进, 送; 运 is to move, then to be moved by luck.
云 (yún) is a near sound match for yùn.
力 (strength) — effort and motion, as in 办, 助, 努. The part 云 stands in for 重 in the traditional 動, which was the sound clue.
贝 (cowry shell, money) — wealth and trade: 财, 费, 买, 货; 员 was a paid member or staff. 员 also sounds out 圆 yuán.

example.hanzi: 那位运动员在奥运会上打破了世界纪录。
example.pinyin: Nà wèi yùndòngyuán zài Àoyùnhuì shàng dǎpò le shìjiè jìlù.
example.english: That athlete broke the world record at the Olympics.
example.fact: Usain Bolt set the current 100-meter world record of 9.58 seconds at the 2009 World Championships in Berlin, a mark that has stood for over 15 years despite advances in training science and shoe technology. At his peak speed, Bolt covered roughly 12.3 meters per second, briefly reaching nearly 44 kilometers per hour. Sports scientists still debate how much faster human sprinters could theoretically go given human muscle and tendon limits.

examples.hanzi: 这位运动员每天训练六个小时。
examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi yùndòngyuán měitiān xùnliàn liù ge xiǎoshí.
examples.english: This athlete trains six hours every day.

examples.hanzi: 运动员们正在热身。
examples.pinyin: Yùndòngyuánmen zhèngzài rèshēn.
examples.english: The athletes are warming up.

components.note: 冏 (bright/window) — the lower part; dictionary treats it as the 'bright' hint. Meaning 'trade, business' is better remembered as a market (商店).
口 (mouth) — dictionary radical, as in 吃 eat. Memory aid: a shop-keeper's mouth calling out prices; 商量 is to 'talk it over'.
Memory aid: 业 looks like a row of upright posts on a base, like a shop sign or an old tool stand; 'business/trade' is the extended meaning. Origin is unclear, so no firm etymology.

example.hanzi: 这座城市因商业发达而闻名。
example.pinyin: Zhè zuò chéngshì yīn shāngyè fādá ér wénmíng.
example.english: This city is famous for its thriving commerce.
example.fact: Venice became one of medieval Europe's great commercial powers by dominating trade routes between Europe and the East, particularly in spices, silk, and glass, from roughly the 9th to 15th centuries. Its merchants developed early forms of double-entry bookkeeping and maritime insurance to manage the risks of long trading voyages. At its height, the Venetian Arsenal could build a fully equipped war galley in under a day using an early form of assembly-line production.

examples.hanzi: 这条街是商业区，人很多。
examples.pinyin: Zhè tiáo jiē shì shāngyè qū, rén hěn duō.
examples.english: This street is a commercial area with lots of people.

examples.hanzi: 他想学习商业管理。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng xuéxí shāngyè guǎnlǐ.
examples.english: He wants to study business management.

components.note: 食 (food, eat) — a lid over a bowl of food. As a left-hand radical it becomes 饣: 饭 meal, 饿 hungry, 饱 full, 饺 dumpling.
口 (mouth) — three mouths: many goods and people speaking; hence products, quality, and to taste. Also in 品尝 and 作品.

example.hanzi: 超市里新上架了很多进口食品。
example.pinyin: Chāoshì lǐ xīn shàngjià le hěn duō jìnkǒu shípǐn.
example.english: The supermarket just stocked a lot of new imported food products.
example.fact: Canned food was invented in the early 1800s to supply the French military under Napoleon, after a contest offered a cash prize for a reliable way to preserve food for troops on long campaigns. Nicolas Appert developed the sealed-jar method in 1809, though the science of why it worked — bacteria being killed by heat and sealed off from air — wasn't understood until Louis Pasteur's germ theory decades later. The can opener wasn't invented until nearly 50 years after canned food itself, so early cans had to be hacked open with a hammer and chisel.

examples.hanzi: 我们要注意食品安全。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào zhùyì shípǐn ānquán.
examples.english: We need to pay attention to food safety.

examples.hanzi: 这家店卖各种冷冻食品。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn mài gèzhǒng lěngdòng shípǐn.
examples.english: This shop sells all kinds of frozen food.

components.note: 自 (self) — picture of a nose; Chinese speakers point to the nose to mean "I", so it became "self" (compare 鼻 bí, nose, which adds 畀).
禾 (grain) — crops: 秋 autumn, 种 plant, 秒 second; 私 was grain held for oneself.
厶 (sī) is the ancient form of 私 itself, meaning private; 公 gōng (public) is its opposite.

example.hanzi: 他总是先考虑自己的利益,大家都觉得他很自私。
example.pinyin: Tā zǒngshì xiān kǎolǜ zìjǐ de lìyì, dàjiā dōu juéde tā hěn zìsī.
example.english: He always considers his own interests first, and everyone thinks he's very selfish.
example.fact: In 1976, evolutionary biologist Richard Dawkins popularized the idea that genes, not individuals or species, are the fundamental unit driving natural selection in his book 'The Selfish Gene.' The theory helped explain altruistic behaviors in animals, such as bees sacrificing themselves for a hive, as strategies that ultimately benefit the survival of shared genes rather than contradicting self-interest. The book remains one of the most influential and widely read works of popular science of the 20th century.

examples.hanzi: 他有点自私，从不分享。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǒudiǎn zìsī, cóng bù fēnxiǎng.
examples.english: He's a bit selfish and never shares.

examples.hanzi: 我觉得这样做对别人太自私了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ juéde zhèyàng zuò duì biéren tài zìsī le.
examples.english: I think doing it this way is too selfish toward others.

components.note: 角 (horn) — an ox's horn; with 刀 (knife) the picture is cutting up an ox, so "to take apart", then to loosen and explain.
刀 (knife) — cutting, as in 分, 切, 到; a blade separates the parts.
廾 (two hands) — in 開 two hands lift the bar of a gate; 开 is the simplified shape. Compare 关 (close).

example.hanzi: 侦探终于解开了这个多年未破的谜案。
example.pinyin: Zhēntàn zhōngyú jiěkāi le zhège duōnián wèi pò de mí'àn.
example.english: The detective finally solved this mystery case that had gone unsolved for years.
example.fact: The Zodiac Killer sent taunting encrypted letters to California newspapers in 1969, and one of his four ciphers, known as Z340, went unsolved for 51 years. In December 2020, a team of amateur codebreakers from the US, Australia, and Belgium finally cracked it using a combination of manual analysis and computer-assisted pattern matching. The decoded message revealed no new clues to the killer's identity, which remains officially unknown.

examples.hanzi: 请帮我解开这个绳子。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng bāng wǒ jiěkāi zhège shéngzi.
examples.english: Please help me untie this rope.

examples.hanzi: 我终于解开了这道数学题。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhōngyú jiěkāi le zhè dào shùxué tí.
examples.english: I finally solved this math problem.

meanings: the seat to the right of the main guest

components.note: 下 (below) — a mark placed under a line, the mirror of 上 above.
手 (hand) — a picture of a hand with fingers spread. As a left-hand radical it becomes 扌 in 打 hit, 拿 take, 推 push.

example.hanzi: 这个项目太复杂了,他不知道该从哪里下手。
example.pinyin: Zhège xiàngmù tài fùzá le, tā bù zhīdào gāi cóng nǎlǐ xiàshǒu.
example.english: This project is too complicated, and he doesn't know where to start.
example.fact: The Apollo 11 moon landing in 1969 required breaking an almost unimaginably complex problem into manageable pieces, ultimately involving over 400,000 engineers, scientists, and technicians across NASA and its contractors. Margaret Hamilton's team at MIT wrote the onboard guidance software largely from scratch, since no reusable code existed for a task like landing on the Moon. Her code famously handled an unexpected computer overload alarm during the actual descent, prioritizing critical landing tasks and allowing the mission to proceed safely.

examples.hanzi: 这么多事情，我不知道从哪儿下手。
examples.pinyin: Zhème duō shìqing, wǒ bù zhīdào cóng nǎr xiàshǒu.
examples.english: With so many things to do, I don't know where to start.

examples.hanzi: 别担心，我先从简单的下手。
examples.pinyin: Bié dānxīn, wǒ xiān cóng jiǎndān de xiàshǒu.
examples.english: Don't worry, I'll start with the easy part.

meanings: (term of endearment for a child) darling

components.note: 北 (north; two people back to back) — in older Chinese 乖 meant 'at odds, contrary' (乖张), which fits two figures turned away; 'well-behaved' is the later colloquial sense.
千 (thousand) — sits on top. Memory aid: no reliable etymology; picture a child with a thousand reasons to misbehave who still stays put.

千 (thousand) — sits on top. Memory aid: no reliable etymology; picture a child with a thousand reasons to misbehave who still stays put.

example.hanzi: 小狗乖乖地坐在主人脚边,一动也不动。
example.pinyin: Xiǎo gǒu guāiguāi de zuò zài zhǔrén jiǎo biān, yī dòng yě bù dòng.
example.english: The little dog sat obediently by its owner's feet, not moving at all.
example.fact: Border collies are widely considered one of the most trainable dog breeds, in part because they were selectively bred for centuries in Scotland and England to herd sheep by responding instantly to subtle whistle and hand signals from a shepherd. A famous 2004 study found a border collie named Rico could correctly identify over 200 different toys by name, and could even learn new object names by process of elimination, a skill previously thought unique to young children. This ability to infer new word meanings without explicit training is called 'fast mapping.'

examples.hanzi: 你要乖乖地听妈妈的话。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ yào guāiguāi de tīng māma de huà.
examples.english: You must listen to Mom obediently.

examples.hanzi: 孩子乖乖地躺在床上睡觉。
examples.pinyin: Háizi guāiguāi de tǎng zài chuáng shàng shuìjiào.
examples.english: The child lay in bed sleeping quietly.

components.note: 门 (gate) — marks gates and doors, as in 问, 间, 闪, 开; 闯 shows a horse 马 bursting through a gate.
马 (horse) — the charging animal, as in 骑 ride, 骂.
辶 (walk) — movement, as in 过, 近, 送: to go forward.
井 stands in for 隹 of 進, a loose clue only.

example.hanzi: 一只野猫突然闯进了教室,吓了大家一跳。
example.pinyin: Yī zhī yěmāo tūrán chuǎngjìn le jiàoshì, xià le dàjiā yī tiào.
example.english: A stray cat suddenly burst into the classroom, startling everyone.
example.fact: Wild animals wandering into unexpected human spaces is more common than most people realize; in cities like Chicago, coyotes have been documented walking into convenience stores and even riding public transit. Urban wildlife researchers attribute this partly to habitat fragmentation pushing animals to navigate through developed areas, and partly to some species adapting remarkably well to city life. Raccoons in particular have been shown in lab studies to solve complex latch-and-lock puzzles, explaining their knack for breaking into secured spaces.

examples.hanzi: 小偷闯进了邻居家里。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎotōu chuǎng jìn le línjū jiā lǐ.
examples.english: A thief broke into the neighbor's home.

examples.hanzi: 你不能随便闯进别人的房间。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bù néng suíbiàn chuǎng jìn biéren de fángjiān.
examples.english: You can't just barge into other people's rooms.

components.note: 扌 (hand radical, 提手旁) — actions by hand: 打, 拉, 抱; 提 is to lift or carry in the hand.
是 (shì) is a loose sound hint; the same part is in 题 tí and 堤 dī.
高 (tall) — a drawing of a tall tower building. 高 also sounds out 糕 gāo (cake), 搞 gǎo and 稿 gǎo.

example.hanzi: 每天坚持锻炼可以提高身体的免疫力。
example.pinyin: Měitiān jiānchí duànliàn kěyǐ tígāo shēntǐ de miǎnyìlì.
example.english: Exercising consistently every day can improve the body's immune function.
example.fact: Regular moderate exercise has been shown in numerous studies to increase circulation of immune cells like natural killer cells and T-lymphocytes, helping the body detect and respond to pathogens faster. A landmark study following marathon runners found that moderate, consistent training reduced the frequency of upper respiratory infections, while extreme overtraining without recovery could temporarily suppress immune function instead. The World Health Organization recommends at least 150 minutes of moderate aerobic activity per week for overall health benefits, including immune support.

examples.hanzi: 这个办法能提高工作效率。
examples.pinyin: Zhège bànfǎ néng tígāo gōngzuò xiàolǜ.
examples.english: This method can improve work efficiency.

examples.hanzi: 我想提高我的汉语水平。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng tígāo wǒ de Hànyǔ shuǐpíng.
examples.english: I want to improve my Chinese level.

components.note: 日 (sun) — time and day, as in 早 early, 时 time, 明 bright; 晚 is when the sun is late.
免 (miǎn) is a close sound clue for wǎn; it also sounds out 勉 miǎn and 挽 wǎn.
灬 (fire) — heat and burning, as in 热 hot, 照 shine, 黑 black; a dot is a small spot like a spark.
占 (zhàn) is a loose sound clue for diǎn; 占 also sounds out 站 zhàn and 粘 zhān.

example.hanzi: 由于大雾,今天的航班晚点了三个小时。
example.pinyin: Yóuyú dà wù, jīntiān de hángbān wǎndiǎn le sān gè xiǎoshí.
example.english: Due to heavy fog, today's flight was delayed by three hours.
example.fact: Fog remains one of aviation's most persistent hazards because it can drop visibility to near zero at ground level even when skies above are clear. London's Heathrow Airport is particularly prone to fog delays due to its location in the Thames Valley, a natural basin where cool, moist air collects overnight. Modern instrument landing systems allow many aircraft to land in extremely low visibility, but fog still frequently forces air traffic controllers to reduce the rate of arrivals for safety, causing cascading delays.

examples.hanzi: 我可能会晚点到，你们先吃吧。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ kěnéng huì wǎndiǎn dào, nǐmen xiān chī ba.
examples.english: I may arrive a bit late, so go ahead and eat first.

examples.hanzi: 我们晚点再聊，好吗？
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen wǎndiǎn zài liáo, hǎo ma?
examples.english: Let's talk a bit later, okay?

components.note: 宀 (roof) — marks houses and shelter, as in 家 home, 室 room, 客 guest; 宰 is a person in the house in charge, then to slaughter, as in 宰相 chief minister.

example.hanzi: 过年的时候，他们宰了一只羊。
example.pinyin: Guònián de shíhou, tāmen zǎi le yì zhī yáng.
example.english: At New Year they slaughtered a sheep.
example.fact: 宰 is the plain verb for slaughtering animals, and slangily it means 'to fleece' a customer: 被宰了 'I got ripped off'. It also appears in 宰相, the ancient 'chancellor' title.

examples.hanzi: 这家店的老板专宰游客。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de lǎobǎn zhuān zǎi yóukè.
examples.english: The owner of this shop rips off tourists.

examples.hanzi: 农场里宰了一头猪。
examples.pinyin: Nóngchǎng li zǎi le yì tóu zhū.
examples.english: They slaughtered a pig on the farm.

components.note: 其 (its) — an old picture of a winnowing basket (箕 jī adds bamboo). Sound clue: 期 qī, 旗 qí, 棋 qí, 欺 qī, 基 jī.
亻 (person) — marks people, as in 你 you, 们 plural, 做 do; 他 is "he" (or other).
也 (yě) is only a loose sound hint for tā; the sibling 她 tā (she) shares it with 女 for woman.
人 (person) — a side-view figure of a person walking. As a radical it appears as 亻 on the left: 你 他 们.

example.hanzi: 除了他以外,其他人都同意这个计划。
example.pinyin: Chúle tā yǐwài, qítārén dōu tóngyì zhège jìhuà.
example.english: Apart from him, everyone else agreed to this plan.
example.fact: The 'bystander effect,' where individuals are less likely to help a victim when other people are present, was first systematically studied after the 1964 murder of Kitty Genovese in New York City. Psychologists John Darley and Bibb Latané ran experiments showing that people are actually more likely to act alone than in a group, because responsibility feels diffused when others are around. The phenomenon has since been replicated in dozens of studies worldwide, though later research revised some early exaggerated claims about the original case's supposed number of witnesses.

examples.hanzi: 他先走了，其他人还在开会。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiān zǒu le, qítā rén hái zài kāihuì.
examples.english: He left first; the others are still in the meeting.

examples.hanzi: 其他人都去哪儿了？
examples.pinyin: Qítā rén dōu qù nǎr le?
examples.english: Where did everyone else go?

components.note: 氵 (water) — 氵 is water, as in 河, 海; sand grains are tiny bits washed by water.
少 (shǎo) — near sound — 沙 is shā; 少 also sounds out 炒 chǎo and 纱 shā.
氵 (water) — marks water and flowing things, as in 河, 海; 漠 is the desert, drained of water, as in 沙漠.
莫 (mò) gives the sound exactly: 漠 mò, also in 膜 mó and 墓 mù.

example.hanzi: 撒哈拉沙漠是世界上最大的热沙漠。
example.pinyin: Sāhālā Shāmò shì shìjiè shàng zuìdà de rè shāmò.
example.english: The Sahara Desert is the largest hot desert in the world.
example.fact: The Sahara covers about 9.2 million square kilometers, roughly the size of the entire United States, and stretches across parts of 11 African countries. Despite its bone-dry reputation today, satellite and sediment studies show the Sahara was lush grassland with lakes and rivers as recently as 6,000 years ago, a period called the African Humid Period. Shifts in Earth's orbital tilt are believed to have triggered the transition to the arid desert seen now.

examples.hanzi: 骆驼是沙漠里的好帮手。
examples.pinyin: Luòtuo shì shāmò lǐ de hǎo bāngshou.
examples.english: Camels are great helpers in the desert.

examples.hanzi: 沙漠里白天很热，晚上很冷。
examples.pinyin: Shāmò lǐ báitiān hěn rè, wǎnshang hěn lěng.
examples.english: In the desert it's hot by day and cold at night.

components.note: 贝 (shell, money) — marks wealth and trade, as in 财 wealth, 贵 expensive; 贼 is the one who steals it.
戎 (róng) — loose sound hint (zéi vs róng); 戎 also means weapon.

example.hanzi: 警察抓到了那个贼。
example.pinyin: Jǐngchá zhuā dào le nàge zéi.
example.english: The police caught that thief.
example.fact: 贼 means 'thief' (a petty thief is more commonly called 小偷 in speech), but northern speakers also use it as a vivid adverb: 贼冷 is 'freezing cold'. A common idiom, 贼喊捉贼, means 'a thief crying thief'.

examples.hanzi: 家里昨晚进了贼。
examples.pinyin: Jiā li zuówǎn jìn le zéi.
examples.english: A thief broke into the house last night.

examples.hanzi: 小贼被警察抓住了。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎozéi bèi jǐngchá zhuā zhù le.
examples.english: The petty thief was caught by the police.

components.note: 木 (wood) — wooden things: 桌, 板, 架; 档 is a wooden shelf for files.
当 (dāng) is a near sound match for dàng; also in 挡 dǎng.

example.hanzi: 我把旧档案放进了柜子里。
example.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ jiù dàng'àn fàng jìn le guìzi lǐ.
example.english: I put the old files into the cabinet.
example.fact: 档 sits in 档案 (files, records), and in grade words like 高档 (high-end) and 低档 (low-end). It also names a time slot, as in 档期 (release window), and in Taiwan it is how the gears of a car are counted.

examples.hanzi: 我找不到那个文档。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhǎo bu dào nàge wéndàng.
examples.english: I can't find that document.

examples.hanzi: 开车时要换档。
examples.pinyin: Kāichē shí yào huàn dàng.
examples.english: You need to shift gears when driving.

components.note: 凯 (kǎi) — triumph, mostly seen in names; as a part it sounds out 铠 kǎi and 恺 kǎi.
文 (writing, culture) — a person with a patterned chest, early tattooed designs, which became writing and culture. Also in 纹 wén and 蚊 wén.

example.hanzi: 我的美国朋友叫凯文,他在纽约工作。
example.pinyin: Wǒ de Měiguó péngyǒu jiào Kǎiwén, tā zài Niǔyuē gōngzuò.
example.english: My American friend is named Kevin, and he works in New York.
example.fact: The name Kevin comes from the Irish 'Caoimhín,' meaning 'handsome' or 'beloved,' and is associated with Saint Kevin of Glendalough, a 6th-century Irish monk. Legend holds that Saint Kevin once held his hand still so long in prayer that a blackbird nested and laid eggs in his palm, and he waited patiently until the chicks hatched and flew away. The name spread well beyond Ireland in the 20th century and became especially popular in the United States after the 1950s.

examples.hanzi: 凯文打算明年去中国学习。
examples.pinyin: Kǎiwén dǎsuàn míngnián qù Zhōngguó xuéxí.
examples.english: Kevin plans to study in China next year.

examples.hanzi: 凯文，你能过来一下吗？
examples.pinyin: Kǎiwén, nǐ néng guòlái yíxià ma?
examples.english: Kevin, can you come over for a moment?

components.note: 手 (hand) — a picture of a hand with fingers spread. As a left-hand radical it becomes 扌 in 打 hit, 拿 take, 推 push.
大 (big/man) — the top part, as in 夫. Dictionary story: a big man wrapped in a long cloth, hence 'cover, set'; used in 外套 coat and 手套 glove.
镸 (long) — the bottom part, a long-hair variant of 長. Memory aid: a long cloth over a big person is a coat or cover.

example.hanzi: 冬天出门时,他总是戴上一副厚厚的手套。
example.pinyin: Dōngtiān chūmén shí, tā zǒngshì dài shàng yī fù hòu hòu de shǒutào.
example.english: When going out in winter, he always puts on a pair of thick gloves.
example.fact: Surgical gloves were introduced in the 1890s at Johns Hopkins Hospital, originally to protect a nurse's hands from harsh antiseptic chemicals rather than to prevent infection transmission, which was only later understood to be a major benefit. Latex rubber gloves became standard practice worldwide by the mid-20th century as germ theory gained wider acceptance in surgical settings. Today the humble disposable glove is manufactured in the hundreds of billions annually, with global demand spiking sharply during the COVID-19 pandemic.

examples.hanzi: 我的手套不见了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de shǒutào bú jiàn le.
examples.english: I've lost my gloves.

examples.hanzi: 外面很冷，记得戴手套。
examples.pinyin: Wàimiàn hěn lěng, jìde dài shǒutào.
examples.english: It's very cold outside, so remember to wear gloves.

components.note: 亻 (person radical, 单人旁) — people and what they do: 你, 他, 位; 偶 first meant a figure or doll, then a pair.
禺 (yú) is a loose sound clue; same part in 遇 yù, 愚 yú, 寓 yù.
⺈ (bent figure) — the top part of 尔, a variant stroke group. 尔 is an old form of 'you'; today it appears mainly in foreign names like 比尔 Bill.
小 (small) — the bottom part and radical, as in 少 few. The shape does not explain 'you'; the character is now mostly sound-borrowed.

example.hanzi: 他平时很少喝咖啡,偶尔才会喝一杯。
example.pinyin: Tā píngshí hěn shǎo hē kāfēi, ǒu'ěr cái huì hē yī bēi.
example.english: He rarely drinks coffee normally, only occasionally having a cup.
example.fact: Coffee is believed to have been discovered in Ethiopia sometime before the 15th century, according to a popular legend about a goat herder named Kaldi who noticed his goats became unusually energetic after eating berries from a certain shrub. From Ethiopia, coffee cultivation spread to Yemen and then across the Islamic world, where coffeehouses became important centers for conversation and the exchange of ideas by the 1500s. Today coffee is one of the most heavily traded agricultural commodities in the world.

examples.hanzi: 我偶尔会去公园散步。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ ǒu'ěr huì qù gōngyuán sànbù.
examples.english: I occasionally go for a walk in the park.

examples.hanzi: 他偶尔也会做饭，但不常做。
examples.pinyin: Tā ǒu'ěr yě huì zuòfàn, dàn bù cháng zuò.
examples.english: He cooks once in a while, but not often.

components.note: 亻 (person) — marks people and their roles, as in 你 you, 们 plural, 信 trust; 亿 is a person, now only used for a hundred million.
乙 (yǐ) — close sound: 亿 yì.

example.hanzi: 中国有十几亿人口。
example.pinyin: Zhōngguó yǒu shí jǐ yì rénkǒu.
example.english: China has over a billion people.
example.fact: 亿 means 100 million, not a billion, because Chinese groups big numbers by 万 (10,000). So 十亿 is a billion and 一百亿 is ten billion; always convert to 万 and 亿 when reading large figures.

examples.hanzi: 地球上有七十多亿人。
examples.pinyin: Dìqiú shang yǒu qīshí duō yì rén.
examples.english: There are over seven billion people on Earth.

examples.hanzi: 这家公司去年赚了一亿元。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī qùnián zhuàn le yí yì yuán.
examples.english: This company earned a hundred million yuan last year.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — crops, as in 秋 autumn, 租 rent, 和 and 秒 second; 种 is seed or to plant.
中 (zhōng) is a close sound clue for zhǒng/zhòng.
矢 (arrow) with a flag 方: a clan or troop gathered under its banner, with arrows at hand.

example.hanzi: 这项政策旨在消除种族之间的不平等。
example.pinyin: Zhè xiàng zhèngcè zhǐzài xiāochú zhǒngzú zhījiān de bù píngděng.
example.english: This policy aims to eliminate inequality between different races.
example.fact: Modern genetics has shown that there is more genetic variation within traditionally defined racial groups than between them, and the American Society of Human Genetics has stated that race is primarily a social construct rather than a rigid biological category. The 2003 completion of the Human Genome Project, which sequenced a full human genome for the first time, reinforced how genetically similar all humans are, sharing about 99.9% of their DNA regardless of ancestry. Population geneticists instead study more precise concepts like ancestry and geographic lineage to understand human genetic diversity.

examples.hanzi: 学校里有来自不同种族的学生。
examples.pinyin: Xuéxiào lǐ yǒu láizì bùtóng zhǒngzú de xuésheng.
examples.english: The school has students from different ethnic backgrounds.

examples.hanzi: 我们应该尊重每一个种族。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yīnggāi zūnzhòng měi yí ge zhǒngzú.
examples.english: We should respect every race.

components.note: ⺈ (bent person) — a person's figure, the top part of 色. Old story: a person (⺈) sitting on 巴 shows how feelings colour the face, hence 'colour, look'; treat as a memory aid.
巴 (bā) — the lower part; dictionary reads the pair as 'what a person desires'. Memory aid: a face reddening with feeling is a 'colour'.
忄 (heart) — feelings, as in 快 happy, 怕 afraid, 忙 busy.
青 (qīng) is a close sound clue for qíng; the series 清 qīng, 请 qǐng, 晴 qíng, 精 jīng.

example.hanzi: 该网站因发布色情内容而被政府关闭。
example.pinyin: Gāi wǎngzhàn yīn fābù sèqíng nèiróng ér bèi zhèngfǔ guānbì.
example.english: The website was shut down by the government for publishing pornographic content.
example.fact: Government regulation of explicit material long predates the internet; the UK's Obscene Publications Act of 1857 was one of the first laws specifically targeting the sale of obscene material, spurred partly by concerns over cheap printed pamphlets. In the United States, the Supreme Court's 1973 Miller v. California ruling established the modern legal test for obscenity, which still shapes how courts evaluate such content today. The rise of the internet has posed persistent jurisdictional challenges for regulators, since content hosted in one country can be accessed almost anywhere else.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们不应该看色情内容。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen bù yīnggāi kàn sèqíng nèiróng.
examples.english: Children shouldn't watch pornographic content.

examples.hanzi: 这个软件可以过滤色情网站。
examples.pinyin: Zhège ruǎnjiàn kěyǐ guòlǜ sèqíng wǎngzhàn.
examples.english: This software can filter pornographic websites.

components.note: 面 (face) — a picture of a face; extended to the surface or side of things, as in 外面 outside.
临 (simplified 臨) — the old form shows a person bending over with a watching eye above a heap of goods: looking down on something, hence 'to face, to draw near'.

example.hanzi: 这个小岛正面临海平面上升带来的威胁。
example.pinyin: Zhège xiǎodǎo zhèng miànlín hǎi píngmiàn shàngshēng dàilái de wēixié.
example.english: This small island is currently facing the threat brought by rising sea levels.
example.fact: The low-lying Pacific nation of Tuvalu, with an average elevation of less than two meters above sea level, is often cited as one of the countries most immediately threatened by rising seas caused by climate change. In 2022, Tuvalu's foreign minister delivered a speech at the COP26 climate conference while standing knee-deep in seawater to dramatize the threat. The country has since begun digitally recreating itself in a virtual model as a contingency in case its physical land eventually becomes uninhabitable.

examples.hanzi: 公司现在面临很大的困难。
examples.pinyin: Gōngsī xiànzài miànlín hěn dà de kùnnan.
examples.english: The company is now facing great difficulties.

examples.hanzi: 他即将面临一个重要的选择。
examples.pinyin: Tā jíjiāng miànlín yí ge zhòngyào de xuǎnzé.
examples.english: He's about to face an important choice.

components.note: ⺮ (bamboo) — bamboo slips arranged in an even row; 等 means "rank, equal" and then "wait".
寺 (sì) is only a loose sound clue for děng; 寺 also in 诗 shī and 持 chí.
于 (yú) is a sound clue for 宇 yǔ and 芋 yù; it is a light grammar word meaning "at, to".

example.hanzi: 一公里等于一千米。
example.pinyin: Yī gōnglǐ děngyú yī qiān mǐ.
example.english: One kilometer equals one thousand meters.
example.fact: The meter was originally defined in 1793 by French scientists as one ten-millionth of the distance from the North Pole to the equator along a meridian through Paris. Since 1983, it has instead been defined using the speed of light: exactly the distance light travels in a vacuum in 1/299,792,458 of a second. This shift let the meter be measured to extraordinary precision anywhere in the world without relying on a physical reference object.

examples.hanzi: 二加二等于四。
examples.pinyin: Èr jiā èr děngyú sì.
examples.english: Two plus two equals four.

examples.hanzi: 不回答等于拒绝。
examples.pinyin: Bù huídá děngyú jùjué.
examples.english: Not answering amounts to refusing.

components.note: 必 (bì) is a sound clue for 秘 mì, 密 mì and 蜜 mì: the same series, with only the initial changing.

example.hanzi: 你不必这么着急。
example.pinyin: Nǐ búbì zhème zháojí.
example.english: You don't need to be in such a hurry.
example.fact: 必 is mostly a formal adverb: 必须 (must), 必然 (inevitable) and 不必 ('need not') are the most common. 必 can also appear as 未必 'not necessarily', a handy phrase for politely disagreeing.

examples.hanzi: 你必须按时完成作业。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ bìxū ànshí wánchéng zuòyè.
examples.english: You must finish your homework on time.

examples.hanzi: 明天不必来这么早。
examples.pinyin: Míngtiān búbì lái zhème zǎo.
examples.english: You don't need to come so early tomorrow.

components.note: 宀 (roof) — a house or building, as in 家, 安, 室; 宫 is a palace, a grand house.

example.hanzi: 我们明天去故宫。
example.pinyin: Wǒmen míngtiān qù Gùgōng.
example.english: We're going to the Forbidden City tomorrow.
example.fact: 宫 refers to a palace, especially an imperial one, so the Beijing Forbidden City is 故宫 ('former palace'). It also names the 子宫 (uterus) and Taoist temples, and is the first note of the traditional five-note scale.

examples.hanzi: 北京有很多古代的宫殿。
examples.pinyin: Běijīng yǒu hěn duō gǔdài de gōngdiàn.
examples.english: Beijing has many ancient palaces.

examples.hanzi: 孩子们在少年宫学画画。
examples.pinyin: Háizimen zài shàoniángōng xué huàhuà.
examples.english: The kids learn drawing at the Children's Palace.

components.note: 走 (walk, run) — marks movement on foot, as in 起 rise, 越 cross, 超 surpass; 赶 is chasing or hurrying to catch up.
干 (gān) — gives the sound — 赶 is gǎn, same syllable with a different tone; 秆 gǎn and 肝 gān share it.
至 (arrive) — 到 is to arrive.
刂 is the knife form 刀 (dāo), a close sound clue for dào; 到 itself sounds out 倒 dǎo/dào.

example.hanzi: 消防员在几分钟内就赶到了火灾现场。
example.pinyin: Xiāofángyuán zài jǐ fēnzhōng nèi jiù gǎndào le huǒzāi xiànchǎng.
example.english: The firefighters arrived at the scene of the fire within just a few minutes.
example.fact: In most major cities, fire departments aim for a response time of under 5-6 minutes from the moment a call is dispatched, since fires can grow roughly ten times larger for every minute of delay in the first phase after ignition. Modern fire stations use computer-aided dispatch systems that automatically identify and route the nearest available truck to minimize travel time. Some cities have also experimented with dispatching lighter, faster rapid-response vehicles ahead of the full engine to begin assessment sooner.

examples.hanzi: 我们赶到车站时，火车已经开了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen gǎndào chēzhàn shí, huǒchē yǐjīng kāi le.
examples.english: By the time we hurried to the station, the train had already left.

examples.hanzi: 他一接到电话就赶到了医院。
examples.pinyin: Tā yì jiēdào diànhuà jiù gǎndào le yīyuàn.
examples.english: As soon as he got the call, he rushed to the hospital.

components.note: 當 (traditional) — 田 field under 尚 (shàng), 尚 being a loose sound hint for dāng. 当 keeps only a squashed top and a few strokes of it.
尚 (shàng) — the top part of 當; only a loose sound clue today. 当 is dāng (to act as, should) or dàng (appropriate).
心 (heart) — a picture of a heart. Written 忄 on the left (快, 怕) and 心 at the bottom (想, 思, 忘); it marks feelings and thoughts.

example.hanzi: 路面很滑,请大家当心脚下。
example.pinyin: Lùmiàn hěn huá, qǐng dàjiā dāngxīn jiǎoxià.
example.english: The road surface is very slippery, so everyone please watch your step.
example.fact: Ice is most dangerously slippery at temperatures just below freezing, around -2°C, because a thin film of liquid-like water forms on its surface even though the bulk ice remains solid — a phenomenon scientists have studied since the 19th century but still debate the exact cause of. This thin film dramatically reduces friction, which is why black ice on roads is especially hazardous since it's nearly invisible against dark asphalt. Many cities apply salt to roads specifically because it lowers the freezing point of water, preventing that slick film from forming as easily.

examples.hanzi: 过马路要当心车辆。
examples.pinyin: Guò mǎlù yào dāngxīn chēliàng.
examples.english: Be careful of vehicles when crossing the road.

examples.hanzi: 你拿着热水，当心烫手。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ ná zhe rèshuǐ, dāngxīn tàng shǒu.
examples.english: You're holding hot water, so watch out for burns.

components.note: 入 (enter) — a pointed shape pushing in; not 人 (person), whose strokes spread outward.
亻 (person) — marks people and their actions, as in 你, 他, 做; 侵 is to encroach, as in 入侵; the right side also sounds out 浸 jìn.

example.hanzi: 这种外来物种的入侵严重破坏了当地的生态系统。
example.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng wàilái wùzhǒng de rùqīn yánzhòng pòhuài le dāngdì de shēngtài xìtǒng.
example.english: The invasion of this foreign species has seriously damaged the local ecosystem.
example.fact: The cane toad was deliberately introduced to Australia in 1935 to control beetles damaging sugar cane crops, but it failed to eat the target pest and instead spread explosively across the continent, since it has no natural predators there and secretes a toxin lethal to most native animals that try to eat it. The population has since grown from around 3,000 released toads to an estimated 200 million or more. Australian researchers have experimented with training native predators like quolls to avoid eating the toads by using smaller, non-lethal doses as an aversion trigger.

examples.hanzi: 这个国家被外国军队入侵了。
examples.pinyin: Zhège guójiā bèi wàiguó jūnduì rùqīn le.
examples.english: This country was invaded by a foreign army.

examples.hanzi: 病毒入侵了我的电脑。
examples.pinyin: Bìngdú rùqīn le wǒ de diànnǎo.
examples.english: A virus invaded my computer.

components.note: 纟 (silk thread, simplified 糸) — threads and cloth, as in 红 red, 给 give, 级 level; 经 first meant a warp thread, then "classics, pass through".
巠 (jīng), here simplified to look like 圣, gives the same sound; also in 茎 jīng, 径 jìng and 轻 qīng.
营 (yíng) — camp, to run a business; as a part it sounds out 荧 yíng, 萤 yíng and 莹 yíng.

example.hanzi: 他辞去工作,开始经营自己的小餐馆。
example.pinyin: Tā cíqù gōngzuò, kāishǐ jīngyíng zìjǐ de xiǎo cānguǎn.
example.english: He quit his job and started running his own small restaurant.
example.fact: McDonald's began in 1940 as a single barbecue restaurant in San Bernardino, California, run by brothers Richard and Maurice McDonald, before they streamlined it into a fast, assembly-line-style burger stand in 1948 called the 'Speedee Service System.' Ray Kroc, who initially joined as a milkshake-machine salesman, later bought the franchising rights and built it into the global chain known today, which now operates in over 100 countries. The company's system of standardized operations and supply chains became a widely studied model for running a business at massive scale.

examples.hanzi: 她在城里经营一家花店。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài chéng lǐ jīngyíng yì jiā huādiàn.
examples.english: She runs a flower shop in the city.

examples.hanzi: 这家公司经营得很成功。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā gōngsī jīngyíng de hěn chénggōng.
examples.english: This company is run very successfully.
